_comment: UNPUMPED / GROUND-STATE cavity control for 05_adding_mirror: same two R=0.5 DBR mirrors and same 4-level dye, but source_pump is removed and the whole population starts in the ground state, with absorption and emission both at lam 0.55. Created 2026-07-30 (user). The dye can only take energy out of the probe, never give it back, so this is the loss-side counterpart to the pumped p150 cavity and the zero-gain reference for the pump ladder. NOTE the parent 05 design starts PRE-INVERTED (N1_0=0, N3_0=30) despite a comment there claiming otherwise -- this design does what its comment says.

reservoir._comment: Isotropic dye-doped medium: uniform n=1.5, no LC constants, no relaxation, no lc_fields.npz; gain via the sted block, now genuinely PUMP-DRIVEN (see sted.N1_0/N3_0 below) via source_pump instead of pre-inverted.

sted._comment: All population starts in the GROUND state (level 1) with no pump: initial_populations = [N1_0, 0, N3_0, 0] = [3, 0, 0, 0]. Absorption (1->4) and emission (3->2) are both at lam 0.55, so the dye sits on the signal line and, with no inversion, is a resonant ABSORBER at the probe wavelength. N1_0 was cut 30 -> 3 on 2026-07-31 after measurement: at 30 the cavity passed only 4.9% of the passive signal AND bleached least (0.08% ground-state depletion at amp 10, vs 0.33% at N1_0=3), because transmission depends on the product SGMA*N1_0 while depletion per molecule rises as the dye thins. N1_0=3 gives 70% transmission and the stronger saturable-absorber response -- both knobs improve together.

source_1._comment: Amplitude 100, not the 10 inherited from the pumped cavity: ground-state depletion grows as amplitude^2 and is only 0.33% at amp 10, i.e. linear. 100 is where the measured response actually departs from linear (+7.4% at N1_0=3, vs +0.7% at amp 30 -- the departure grows as amplitude squared. Note most generators override this anyway -- harmonics defaults to --amps 1.0 per tone -- so the drive must be raised on the generator command line too, not just here.

pop_monitor._comment: Atom-level sensor: saves N(t) for all 4 dye levels over the reservoir; snap_interval in MEEP time units (1 unit = 3.336 fs)

n2f_map._comment: | 2026-07-30: n_points 200x200 -> 2x200. The generators read only the LAST column (EH[-1,:]) and xs=linspace(cx-w/2,cx+w/2,nx) puts that column at the same x for nx=2 as for nx=200, so the readout is byte-identical while the far-field transform costs ~200x less (was ~40 min/sample).

mirror_1._comment: Quarter-wave DBR (SimpleSim Mirror object, added 2026-07-29): SiO2/TiO2 n=[1.46, 2.4] at the signal wavelength. reflectivity 0.5 -> 4 layers, achieved R = 0.576 (quantised upward; stored on the object). Two of these around the reservoir form the Fabry-Perot cavity for the memory-reservoir experiments; R is the memory-depth knob.

mirror_2._comment: Quarter-wave DBR (SimpleSim Mirror object, added 2026-07-29): SiO2/TiO2 n=[1.46, 2.4] at the signal wavelength. reflectivity 0.5 -> 4 layers, achieved R = 0.576 (quantised upward; stored on the object). Two of these around the reservoir form the Fabry-Perot cavity for the memory-reservoir experiments; R is the memory-depth knob.

point_snap._comment: Ey time trace at a point in guide_2 (dt=0.1 -> ~5 samples per optical period): the lasing-threshold check. With the CW pump on the whole run, the field after the signal pulse must RING DOWN; growth or a plateau means net round-trip gain >= 1 (lasing) and the operating point is unusable as a memory reservoir.
